identity.what_it_is: NYC Parks 'Coney Island Beach & Boardwalk' (Corbin Pl. to W. 37 St., Brooklyn), nearly 3 miles of beach.
aliases: Brighton Beach (in Fox 5's list of the eight city beaches)
identity.warnings: Fox 5 lists 'Brighton Beach, featuring Coney Island boardwalk' (W 37th St to Ocean Parkway) and has no separate Coney Island entry. Orchard Beach rules (G13-G15) are the Orchard Beach page only. Manhattan Beach and Midland Beach BBQ statements (G17) are not Coney Island rules. The Comptroller text in the bundle is truncated and never mentions Coney Island by name.

spike_candidates.statement: Of the three named Coney boardwalk restrooms, only the Brighton 1 Rd-2 St one is listed wheelchair accessible and it lists no changing tables; W 27 St and W 33 St list one table per room.
spike_candidates.tension: A parent or wheelchair user cannot tell from the city pages which restroom serves both needs.

spike_candidates.statement: The West 27th Street women's room failed its structural check on June 13, 2025, while the park as a whole scores 87.
spike_candidates.tension: The city's own inspection page shows a failing item while the park overall scores 87.

spike_candidates.statement: In 2019 the Comptroller found 73% of NYC park comfort stations had no baby-changing station and only 31% were ADA accessible; Coney's 2025 dataset lists 6 of 8 zones with changing stations.
spike_candidates.tension: Coney's beach restroom zones look better than the citywide 2019 picture, but only 2 of 8 zones are year-round.

facts.fact: NYC Parks lists a Coney Island Beach & Boardwalk public restroom on the Boardwalk between Brighton 1 Rd. and Brighton 2 St., and marks it wheelchair accessible.
facts.quote: coney island boardwalk east between brighton 1 rd. and brighton 2 st. in coney island beach & boardwalk brooklyn wheelchair accessible
facts.source_title: Coney Island Beach & Boardwalk Public Restroom (NYC Parks)

facts.fact: The Brighton 1 Rd.-2 St. restroom has 4 toilets and 8 sinks in the men's room and the same in the women's room; the changing-table count is blank ('--') in both.
facts.quote: men's room number of toilets: 4 number of sinks: 8 number of changing tables: --
facts.source_title: Coney Island Beach & Boardwalk Public Restroom (NYC Parks)

facts.fact: The women's room at the Brighton 1 Rd.-2 St. restroom also has 4 toilets, 8 sinks and no changing-table figure.
facts.quote: women's room number of toilets: 4 number of sinks: 8 number of changing tables: --
facts.source_title: Coney Island Beach & Boardwalk Public Restroom (NYC Parks)

facts.fact: Both rooms at the Brighton 1 Rd.-2 St. restroom were last inspected on August 27, 2024 and rated acceptable on every line (overall, amenities, graffiti, litter, structural).
facts.quote: structural: acceptable last updated: august 27, 2024 women's room
facts.source_title: Coney Island Beach & Boardwalk Public Restroom (NYC Parks)

facts.fact: The West 27th Street restroom is on the Boardwalk at West 27th Street. Its page does not say wheelchair accessible (the Brighton page does carry that line).
facts.quote: boardwalk at west 27th street in coney island beach & boardwalk brooklyn
facts.source_title: West 27th Street Public Restroom (NYC Parks)

facts.fact: West 27th Street: men's room 2 toilets, 2 sinks, 1 changing table; women's room 4 toilets, 2 sinks, 1 changing table.
facts.quote: women's room number of toilets: 4 number of sinks: 2 number of changing tables: 1
facts.source_title: West 27th Street Public Restroom (NYC Parks)

facts.fact: On June 13, 2025 the West 27th Street women's room was rated 'unacceptable' on structural condition (other lines acceptable); the men's room was rated acceptable on all lines.
facts.quote: litter: acceptable structural: unacceptable last updated: june 13, 2025
facts.source_title: West 27th Street Public Restroom (NYC Parks)

facts.fact: West 33rd Street restroom is on the Boardwalk at West 33rd Street, with 2 toilets, 2 sinks and 1 changing table in the men's room.
facts.quote: men's room number of toilets: 2 number of sinks: 2 number of changing tables: 1
facts.source_title: West 33rd Street Public Restroom (NYC Parks)

facts.fact: West 33rd Street women's room has 4 toilets, 2 sinks and 1 changing table; the page says boardwalk at West 33rd Street.
facts.quote: boardwalk at west 33rd street in coney island beach & boardwalk brooklyn
facts.source_title: West 33rd Street Public Restroom (NYC Parks)

facts.fact: West 33rd Street men's room was last inspected August 6, 2025 and the women's room June 26, 2024; all lines acceptable in both rooms.
facts.quote: structural: acceptable last updated: june 26, 2024 facilities
facts.source_title: West 33rd Street Public Restroom (NYC Parks)

facts.fact: NYC Open Data lists 8 Coney Island Beach restroom zones (2a, 2b, 4b, 5a, 5b, 6b, 7a, 7c), all operated by NYC Parks, all Operational, all Fully Accessible, all 8am-4pm 'Open later seasonally'. The dataset names zones, not the three named boardwalk restrooms; do not map them one-to-one.
facts.quote: Coney Island Beach Zone 2a: operator NYC Parks; status Operational; open Year Round; hours 8am-4pm, Open later seasonally; accessibility Fully Accessible; changing stations No.
facts.source_title: NYC Open Data restroom facilities (Coney Island Beach zones)

facts.fact: Only two of the eight Coney Island Beach restroom zones are listed year-round: Zone 2a and Zone 5a. The other six (2b, 4b, 5b, 6b, 7a, 7c) are seasonal.
facts.quote: Coney Island Beach Zone 5a: operator NYC Parks; status Operational; open Year Round; hours 8am-4pm, Open later seasonally; accessibility Fully Accessible; changing stations Yes.
facts.source_title: NYC Open Data restroom facilities (Coney Island Beach zones)

facts.fact: Six of the eight zones list changing stations (2b, 4b, 5a, 5b, 7a, 7c); Zones 2a and 6b list none.
facts.quote: Coney Island Beach Zone 6b: operator NYC Parks; status Operational; open Seasonal; hours 8am-4pm, Open later seasonally; accessibility Fully Accessible; changing stations No.
facts.source_title: NYC Open Data restroom facilities (Coney Island Beach zones)

facts.fact: The Orchard Beach rules page (Bronx only, not Coney Island) bans alcohol, and bans dogs except service animals on the beach and promenade from Memorial Day weekend to Oct. 1. Scope: Orchard Beach.
facts.quote: dogs, except service animals, on beach and promenade from memorial day weekend to oct. 1 consumption of alcohol
facts.source_title: Orchard Beach Rules & Regulations (NYC Parks)

facts.fact: Orchard Beach rules ban barbecuing and open flame except in designated areas. Scope: Orchard Beach only; not a Coney Island rule.
facts.quote: barbecuing and open flame except in designated areas
facts.source_title: Orchard Beach Rules & Regulations (NYC Parks)

facts.fact: Orchard Beach rules say swimming is allowed only with a lifeguard on duty, red flags mean no swimming, and glass containers are banned on the beach and promenade. Scope: Orchard Beach page only.
facts.quote: glass containers are not allowed on the beach or promenade.
facts.source_title: Orchard Beach Rules & Regulations (NYC Parks)

facts.fact: Fox 5 (citing NYC Parks) says alcohol and dogs (service animals excepted) are not permitted on the city's beaches. It states this for all eight beaches, with no Coney-specific wording and no Memorial Day-Oct 1 qualifier for dogs.
facts.quote: alcoholic beverages and dogs, barring service animals, are not permitted on the beaches.
facts.source_title: A closer look at NYC's eight public beaches (Fox 5 NY)

facts.fact: Fox 5 says barbecuing near the beach is allowed at Manhattan Beach and Midland Beach. These are not Coney Island statements. No source here says whether barbecuing is allowed at Coney Island Beach.
facts.quote: barbecuing near the beach is allowed and even encouraged.
facts.source_title: A closer look at NYC's eight public beaches (Fox 5 NY)

facts.fact: In 2025, all eight NYC public beaches opened May 24 and stayed open through September 7, with summer hours of 10 a.m. to 6 p.m. and all described as accessible.
facts.quote: all beaches are open from 10 a.m. to 6 p.m. during summer, and they are all accessible.
facts.source_title: A closer look at NYC's eight public beaches (Fox 5 NY)

facts.fact: Fox 5 describes Brighton Beach (with the Coney Island Boardwalk) as running from West 37th Street to Ocean Parkway and says it has metered parking. The article gives no lot names, rates or hours.
facts.quote: brighton beach has metered parking.
facts.source_title: A closer look at NYC's eight public beaches (Fox 5 NY)

facts.fact: Fox 5 says Manhattan Beach (on Oriental Blvd., Ocean Ave. to Mackenzie St., next to Brighton Beach) has paid parking.
facts.quote: manhattan beach's parking is paid.
facts.source_title: A closer look at NYC's eight public beaches (Fox 5 NY)

facts.fact: NYC Parks describes Coney Island Beach & Boardwalk as Corbin Pl. to W. 37 St. with nearly 3 miles of sandy beach.
facts.quote: with nearly 3 miles of sandy beaches
facts.source_title: Coney Island Beach & Boardwalk (NYC Parks)

facts.fact: NYC Parks gives Coney Island Beach & Boardwalk a park condition score of 87 and $37.6 million in recent investment; the park manager's phone is (718) 946-1353.
facts.quote: 87 park condition score $37.6m recent investment
facts.source_title: Coney Island Beach & Boardwalk (NYC Parks)

facts.fact: The MTA approved a fare increase taking subway, bus and Access-A-Ride from $2.90 to $3 in January 2026; reduced fare rose from $1.45 to $1.50. (Sources are 2025 reports of the planned change, not a 2026 confirmation.)
facts.quote: subway, bus and access-a-ride fares rise 10 cents to $3.
facts.source_title: MTA hiking bus, subway fares to $3 next year (CBS New York)

facts.fact: CBS: as of 2026 the OMNY 7-day fare cap is permanent at $35 on a rolling basis for subway and bus; the first 12 rides are charged, the rest free; $17.50 for reduced-fare riders.
facts.quote: no customer will pay more than $35 for subway and bus rides per seven days on a rolling basis.
facts.source_title: MTA hiking bus, subway fares to $3 next year (CBS New York)

facts.fact: CBS: weekly, monthly and express-bus-plus MetroCard unlimited passes are retired in favor of the fare cap, all payment moves to tap-to-ride, and coins stop being accepted on buses later in 2026; OMNY card fee rises from $1 to $2.
facts.quote: all payment will move to tap-to-ride. no coins will be accepted on buses as of later in 2026.
facts.source_title: MTA hiking bus, subway fares to $3 next year (CBS New York)

facts.fact: ABC7 (July 2025, a plan before the vote) said the OMNY cap would be $36 per seven days, up from $34, and the base fare would go from $2.90 to $3 on Jan. 4, 2026. This conflicts with CBS's $35 (G25); CBS (September 30, 2025, after approval) is newer.
facts.quote: fares on the omny system will be capped at $36 for a seven-day period, up from $34.
facts.source_title: MTA plans to increase subway and bus fares to $3 in January (ABC7 New York)

facts.fact: ABC7: subway and bus fares last rose in 2023, from $2.75 to $2.90.
facts.quote: the subway and bus fares last went up in 2023, when they rose from $2.75 to the current fare of $2.90.
facts.source_title: MTA plans to increase subway and bus fares to $3 in January (ABC7 New York)

facts.fact: The Comptroller's 2019 report counted 1,428 NYC park bathrooms citywide and found nearly 400 damaged or missing features and over 50 hazards at the latest inspections. This is citywide, not Coney-specific.
facts.quote: among the 1,428 nyc parks bathrooms, nearly 400 sinks, toilets, walls, ceilings, changing tables, and other features were damaged or missing during their latest inspection.
facts.source_title: Discomfort Stations (NYC Comptroller, June 27, 2019)

facts.fact: The 2019 report found only 31% of NYC park comfort stations ADA accessible, 11% not open year-round and 73% without infant/toddler changing stations (citywide).
facts.quote: a paltry 31 percent of comfort stations in the five boroughs are ada accessible, 11 percent are not open year-round, and 73 percent do not have changing stations for infants and toddlers.
facts.source_title: Discomfort Stations (NYC Comptroller, June 27, 2019)

facts.fact: The 2019 report put NYC at 16 park bathrooms per 100,000 residents, 93rd of the 100 largest US cities.
facts.quote: this ranks new york an embarrassing 93 rd among the country's 100 largest cities.
facts.source_title: Discomfort Stations (NYC Comptroller, June 27, 2019)

facts.fact: The 2019 report found 100 city bathrooms 'unacceptable' at their latest inspection, including 12 percent of bathrooms in Brooklyn (15 percent in Manhattan). Coney Island is not named in the visible text.
facts.quote: this included 15 percent of nyc parks bathrooms in manhattan and 12 percent in brooklyn
facts.source_title: Discomfort Stations (NYC Comptroller, June 27, 2019)

facts.fact: The report ties the comfort station to the 1930s park buildout under Mayor La Guardia and Commissioner Moses.
facts.quote: in the 1930s, as new york city embarked on a massive buildout of its park system, one feature was central to these efforts: the comfort station.
facts.source_title: Discomfort Stations (NYC Comptroller, June 27, 2019)

facts.fact: NYC Parks' horseshoe crab page says horseshoe crabs have been around for more than 300 million years.
facts.quote: horseshoe crabs have been around for more than 300 million years
facts.source_title: NYC Parks — Horseshoe Crabs in New York City Parks

facts.fact: NYC Parks' Coney Island Creek natural area page says the horseshoe crab has been around roughly 1.2 billion years.
facts.quote: the horseshoe crab has been around since before the dinosaurs, roughly 1.2 billion years
facts.source_title: NYC Parks — Coney Island Creek natural area

facts.fact: After the MTA board vote (reported by ABC7, Sept. 30, 2025), subway and bus fares rose 10 cents from $2.90 to $3, expected to take effect January 4, 2026.
facts.quote: subway and bus fares will increase 10 cents from $2.90 to $3. the change is expected to take effect in january 4, 2026.
facts.source_title: ABC7 NY — MTA board approves proposed subway and bus fare hikes

facts.fact: The approved seven-day unlimited subway and bus price rose from $34 to $35, $1 less than the $36 first proposed.
facts.quote: the seven-day unlimited subway and bus ride prices will increase from $34 to $35, but that is down $1 from the initial planned increase to $36.
facts.source_title: ABC7 NY — MTA board approves proposed subway and bus fare hikes

recency.newest_item: West 33rd Street men's room inspection August 6, 2025; Fox 5 beach guide May 25, 2025; CBS fare article September 30, 2025; NYC Parks page footer lists Council members current in 2026.

dead_ends: No Coney Island Beach rules page: alcohol, dogs, glass, barbecuing, smoking for Coney Island specifically are NOT in any source here (only Orchard Beach's page and Fox 5's citywide summary).
Restroom hours for the three named boardwalk restrooms; whether each is year-round or seasonal (the dataset has zones, not names).
Which Open Data zones correspond to Brighton 1 Rd-2 St, W 27 St and W 33 St.
Parking: no lot names, rates, or hours for Coney Island beach; only 'metered' for Brighton Beach and 'paid' for Manhattan Beach.
Whether the Jan 2026 fare and $35 cap actually took effect as planned (only 2025 reports of the plan).
Any Comptroller finding naming Coney Island; bundle text is truncated mid-chart.
Subway/bus route names, travel times and station names for reaching Coney Island.
conflicts: OMNY 7-day cap: $35 (G25, CBS, Sept 30 2025, after MTA approval) vs $36 (G27, ABC7, July 31 2025, proposed plan). CBS is newer. CBS also says 'first 12 rides are charged', which at $3 would equal $36, so the $35 vs 12-ride wording is itself inconsistent.

Dogs on city beaches: Fox 5 (G17) says not permitted on the beaches generally; Orchard Beach rules page (G14) bans them only from Memorial Day weekend to Oct. 1. Neither is a Coney Island source. Official NYC Parks page wins for its own beach.
Beach naming: NYC Parks calls it Coney Island Beach & Boardwalk (Corbin Pl. to W. 37 St., G22); Fox 5 lists 'Brighton Beach' from West 37th St to Ocean Parkway (G20) and no Coney entry.
West 27th St page lacks a 'wheelchair accessible' line (G05) while Open Data lists all Coney zones 'Fully Accessible' (G11); unresolved because the restroom-to-zone mapping is unknown.
Weekly cap $35 (CBS, G25) vs $36 (ABC7 earlier, G27) RESOLVED by G37: $36 was the initial proposal; the board approved $35.
